newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened slightly against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies after Tuesday's intervention by the Bank of Israel, dealers said.
On Tuesday the Bank bought foreign currency just before the close of the trading day and after the representative rate was published. It was the first intervention in six months.

"The shekel was stable during the whole day and activity was relatively low. When the session opened, the basket was traded at 7.03 percent below the slope but then the shekel started falling following the rise of the dollar abroad," said a dealer at Discount Bank.
The shekel can fluctuate in a band of 7.0 percent above or below a so-called slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
If the shekel-basket rate reaches the lower trading band, the central bank has to intervene by buying foreign currency.
"Yesterday's intervention was on a very low scale but it was enough and the central bank did not have to intervene again today," the dealer added.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1410 versus 3.1370 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5392 shekels versus 3.5385 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8989 shekels per 100 yen versus 2.9104 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.1243 shekels per mark versus 2.1266 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1395 shekels.
